topic: Discrete Convolutions: The Art of Signal Blending

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Echo Effect
lecture_lines: A clap echoes in a concert hall.
The hall's geometry defines the echo.
This echo is a mathematical convolution.
Inputs blend with the system's memory.
We see this through signal reverberation.

Animate a delayed echo wave in magenta (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics: The Sliding Window
lecture_lines: Convolution is a sliding window operation.
Flip one sequence, then shift it.
Multiply overlapping values at each step.
Sum the products to get output.
Repeat this for every output point.
animations: Display a signal array in light gray (#D3D3D3).
Show a window box [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/window.svg] moving across the array in yellow (#FFFF00).
Highlight the current window sum in green (#00FF00).

sections.title: Visualizing Convolution: The 'Blur' Filter
lecture_lines: Filters act as local processing windows.
Slide the kernel over image pixels.
Kernel values modify neighboring pixel data.
animations: Display a 2D image grid in white (#FFFFFF) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg].
Slide a filter matrix over the image in red (#FF0000).
Show the resulting blurred pixels in blue (#0000FF) captured by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg].
